newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts half year net profit falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts half year net profit falls.

text.p: Bakery group Arnotts Ltd said on Friday its profit after tax but before abnormnals was A$33.2 million for the half year ended January 24, a 14.2 percent fall on the previous half to end-December 1995.
Arnotts also declared a dividend of 12 cents.
The company released interim half year results, and said the full detailed stock exchange announcement would be released on March 12.
Arnotts, which has changed its year-end date, said a comparison of like months, including the seasonally low month of January, showed profits after tax had declined just 0.2 percent.
Net profit after abnormals was A$8.5 million, against A$38.66 million in the previous corresponding half.
Sales revenue for the period was A$343.5 million, down 3.9 percent on the previous reported half year, but up 1.4 percent when comparing like months, the company said.
Arnotts said abnormal costs, previously advised to shareholders, came in at A$24.7 million after tax.
The costs relate to a restructuring programme, which was introduced by new management last year and was aimed at revitalising the core domestic business to fuel growth.

"The result for the half-year in a flat Australian retail market, and bearing in mind Arnotts' major resturucturing now well under way, was satisfactory," said Arnotts managing director Chris Roberts in a statement.
Arnotts, which is about 70 percent owned by the Campbell Soup Co, said it expected annual savings of A$10 million after tax from the restructuring program by 1998.
The dividend was unchanged on the previous half year.
